definition.simple: How much you plan to gain compared with how much you plan to lose on a trade.
definition.balanced: Reward to risk = distance to [[take-profit]] ÷ distance to [[stop-loss]]. A 2:1 trade aims to make twice what it risks. A bigger ratio needs a lower [[win-rate]] to break even, but price may reach the target less often.

example: Stop 30 pips away, target 60 pips away: reward to risk is 60 ÷ 30 = 2, written 2:1.
